scope: Primary references for the R1–R4, P1 and G6 manuscript; observed source limits retained.

references.title: Priority Effects in Experimental Pond Communities: Competition between Bufo and Rana
references.use: Introduction: experimental arrival order in amphibian competition.
references.limit: Does not test salamander predation, vegetation interactions or independently manipulated aquatic duration.

references.title: Top predators and habitat complexity alter an intraguild predation module in pond communities
references.use: Discussion: habitat-complexity effects depend on predator identity and salamander intraguild context.
references.limit: Frogs were not experimental prey; no universal vegetation benefit. Issue year 2016, online year 2015.

references.title: Co-occurrence is not evidence of ecological interactions
references.use: Introduction: spatial association does not identify interaction mechanisms.
references.limit: The current response is acoustic activity versus suitability, not measured predator–prey co-occurrence.

references.title: Nonconsumptive effects in a multiple predator system reduce the foraging efficiency of a keystone predator
references.use: Introduction: dragonfly-induced tadpole refuge use can reduce adult-newt foraging.
references.limit: Leaf-litter amount was held constant; newts were adults. This is not a vegetation-dose intervention or salamander-larva behavioural effect.

references.title: WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas
references.use: SI S2: WorldClim citation requested by the version-2.1 provider; fitted rasters use 10-arc-minute BIO1/4/12/15.
references.limit: Product-title 1-km resolution is not the resolution used here; 1970–2000 normals are not survey-day weather.

references.title: North American Amphibian Monitoring Program (NAAMP) anuran detection data from the eastern and central United States (1994–2015)
references.use: Main R1 and data availability: source release of acoustic observations and site coordinates; retained cohort independently verified as 2001–2015.
references.limit: Release spans 1994–2015; that range must not replace the retained analytical range. No direct larval abundance or predation measurements.

references.title: Pattern-oriented modelling: a ‘multi-scope’ for predictive systems ecology
references.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
references.use: Introduction: patterns constrain candidate mechanisms; demographic consequences are tested separately.
references.limit: Does not turn idealized sign compatibility into complete empirical calibration or a field-conditioned posterior.

references.title: You can’t run but you can hide: refuge use in frog tadpoles elicits density-dependent predation by dragonfly larvae
references.use: Introduction: leaf-litter structure alters the density dependence of dragonfly predation on tadpoles.
references.limit: Does not show vegetation-assisted dragonfly predation on frogs or calibrate either model vegetation flag.

references.title: Top-down effects on antagonistic inducible defense and offense
references.use: Introduction: dragonfly risk cues alter larval salamander traits and mediate effects on tadpoles.
references.limit: No vegetation manipulation or NAAMP-taxon calibration; distinguish salamander-mediated changes from Davenport's tadpole refuge use.

references.title: Disentangling the nonlinear effects of habitat complexity on functional responses
references.use: Introduction: artificial vegetation can increase dragonfly attack rates on planktonic invertebrate prey.
references.limit: Prey were Chaoborus larvae, not tadpoles. Exact frog attack support and simultaneous salamander effects remain model assumptions. Detailed claims limited to primary abstract and author-deposited data description.

references.title: Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python
references.use: SI S2: credits the actual scikit-learn implementation, version 1.6.1 in the frozen workflow.
references.limit: No DOI on the primary JMLR record; do not fabricate one. 85 is the JMLR article index.

references.title: Sample selection bias and presence-only distribution models: implications for background and pseudo-absence data
references.use: Main Methods R1 and SI S2: target-group versus uniform-background sensitivity.
references.limit: Does not establish shared sampling bias for all guild members, confirm background absences or imply MaxEnt was fitted.

references.title: Global biotic interactions: An open infrastructure to share and analyze species-interaction datasets
references.use: Data provenance and SI: GloBI indexes interaction literature used in candidate/source review.
references.limit: Index evidence is not contemporaneous pond predation or an empirically fitted attack rate; original contributors retain attribution.

references.title: Linking phenological shifts to species interactions through size-mediated priority effects
references.use: Introduction: size-mediated priority effects among larval dragonflies.
references.limit: Initial size/instar differences were manipulated; do not claim an arrival-day by aquatic-duration experiment or validation of P1's salamander effect.

references.title: Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
references.use: Main R1 and SI S2: structured validation and separate SDM versus acoustic fold designs.
references.limit: 2-degree blocks are not a guarantee of spatial independence or a distance-buffered validation.

references.title: A global 1-km consensus land-cover product for biodiversity and ecosystem modelling
references.use: Main R1 and SI S2: EarthEnv full version 1, including class 8 landscape flooded vegetation and class 12 open water.
references.limit: Landscape consensus prevalence is not submerged-stem structure, hydroperiod or survey-year pond vegetation.
